experiment.scope: The raw WebGPU and Three.js constructions implement the same static full-screen 32-light GGX plus ACES task. Shader wrappers and measured command topology are renderer-specific outcomes.

cpuGpuTraffic.caveat: API-observed logical transfer volume. It is not a PCIe or unified-memory bus trace, and GPU-internal copies are reported separately from CPU↔GPU transfers.

cpuToGpuQueueWrites.byteSemantics: Buffer bytes are API payload bytes; texture bytes are known-format logical texel/block payload and exclude row padding and driver transfers.

externalImageCopies.byteSemantics: Known-format destination logical texel/block payload estimate.

gpuInternalCopies.byteSemantics: Known logical copy payload; texture copies exclude layout padding and unknown formats are counted separately.

gpuToCpuMapReads.byteSemantics: Requested mapped range, counted once at mapAsync; getMappedRange is not added again.

mappedWrites.byteSemantics: CPU-writable mapped capacity; JavaScript writes within a mapped range are not observable, so this is not confirmed transfer volume.

resourceAllocation.caveat: Descriptor-based application allocation estimate; excludes browser/driver overhead, swapchain images, and physical residency.

architectureControl.verdict: The controlled task and dimensions match. Differences in observed API traffic, CPU encoding, command topology, and pacing describe these raw-WebGPU and Three.js renderer constructions on this workload; they do not prove general authoring-system superiority.
